While improved conservation measures such as redesign of rates should be pursued vigorously, the uncertainties of the effects of specific rate redesigns and other conservation measures on the load characteristics of an electric system, the time lag associated with consumer responses, and the long times required for constructing new capacity, severely reduce the practical potential of rate revision and conservation as alternatives, at this time, to the scheduling of projected needed additional generating capacity. Accordingly, these measures cannot be considered as reasonable alternatives to the proposed Bad Creek Project.
8.2.8 Purchase of Power
The Applicant is a member of the Virginia-Carolinas Subregion (VACAR) of the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC). The April 1976 SERC Report on the Coordinated Bulk Power Supply Program shows a forecast VACAR capacity reserve of 5,019 megawatts during the 1983 summer peak. This is only 12.3 percent of the forecast load responsibility. The corresponding reserve which is forecast for the summer of 1984 is 5,982 megawatts, 13.8 percent of the summer peak-load responsibility forecast for that year. In 1985, the forecast summer peak reserve margin is only 10.8 percent. Reserve margins within or above the range 18 to 22 percent 1/ are recommended by SERC for acceptable values of loss-of-load probability. The values forecast for VACAR for the period 1983 to 1985, and given above, are all below this range. Cancellations and slippage in construction schedules can further reduce these reserve margins. In view of the low reserve margins predicted for the VACAR Subregion, it appears that the purchase of capacity equal to that of Bad Creek will be impossible within the subregion. It is noted that the large summer peaks within VACAR are attributable to air-conditioning loads and are therefore coincident.
The purchase of power from the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) would require the construction of long, high-capacity transmission lines. The 1976 SERC Report states that the reserve margins within the TVA service area during the period 1976-1981 will be less than desired. A footnote to Table II(b), which is a listing of TVA's scheduled generator additions, states "units listed for installation beyond five or six years may be largely speculative and are listed as scheduled for convenience only."
